title: Seated Ball Control Circuit
description: A low-impact ball-control circuit done seated or on one knee, isolating hand speed and touch without the legs doing any of the work.

content.objective: Isolate hand speed and ball control without the legs compensating for weak hands.
content.setup: Each player sits on the floor or kneels on one knee with a ball.
instructions: Dribble the ball rapidly between the legs for 20 seconds.
Dribble in a figure-eight around the body for 20 seconds.
Pound the ball hard and low with one hand for 15 seconds, then switch hands.
Finish with 15 seconds of fast alternating hand taps on top of the ball.
coachingPoints: Use only the fingers and wrist, not the whole arm.
Keep the ball low and under control at all times.
Keep the eyes up once the pattern is comfortable.
commonMistakes: Letting the ball bounce too high between touches.
Using the palm instead of the fingertips.
Letting the off-hand drop instead of staying ready to protect the ball.
content.safety: Make sure the floor space is clear before sitting or kneeling down.
